title: Survival Mode Season 2: Titan's Training Sim
summary: Titan’s Training Sim is a Survival Mode 2.0 instance taking place in the Titans Tower.

sections.title: Overview
items: Titan’s Training Sim is a Survival Mode 2.0 instance taking place in the Titans Tower.
Progress points are given after every two rounds and after round 10 the adds and bosses appear again, but with higher CR.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: The Teen Titans are looking for the best of the best to run their new Advanced Holographic Technology through its paces. Think you've got what it takes?

sections.title: General Tips
items: It's a marathon, not a sprint. More DPS = shorter fights = less time for mistakes to happen, but max DPS doesn't equate to cleanest/safest. I've found a balanced approach is best.

You don't need to be some meta DW flurry spam group to do well. SM is all "about passing the exam," ie. knowing the mechanics and doing them. The better you do the mechanics, the easier your life is to the point you can completely trivialize most of the bosses. Mechanics come first, always.

The DPS doesn't need to be max CR/SP as long as they're good at the mechanics and can do good damage regardless. The supports, especially the tank, should be, as you really want the toughest shields you can get your hands on. That said, the tank is the most important and beyond that there's a lot more flexibility. Don't think you can't do SM if you aren't maxed out yet.
Robot Sidekick (and pets in general) is your best friend in here
Manacles of Force is worth thoughtful consideration

Additional tip that virtually everyone has overlooked: Lazarus Pit Water is OP af in SM, especially in the longer, higher rounds where it's basically up as often as you need it to be and it has the potential to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat where you'd otherwise lose 40+ minutes of work. With the potential exception of DPS vs Vampire Lord (due to the soft DPS checks on his shadow pets), the more people who can run it the better. I keep it in my primary boss loadouts then have backup "He is Risen" loadouts that I quick swap to to replace Lazarus w w/e artifact I want. Don't just insta-pop it though; do revives like normal with Water as a last resort, to be popped at the last second if it's in doubt that someone can reach the cog in time. Even if you know you're going to die as soon as you get up, you'll still get another 10s window where hopefully a teammate can revive you.

sections.title: Tank Build
items: Tank is the most critical role in SM and, in addition to knowing the bossfights to a tee, you should be built to maximize your chances of success. Since that's heavily PVP dependent with no sustained blocking and no adds (that you're ultimately responsible for) outside of trash waves, that means your tank build's gonna be a lot different.
Head: If you're Super Speed, and using it, Energized Dash Attack is ideal. Otherwise this is player's choice.

Neck: Fortified Assault, with extra in your inventory in case you want to switch to Fortified Blocking for Ultraman (if his lunge combos are messing you up more than his ranged attacks). Overall, Fortified Assault is BiS in SM since we spend most of our time kiting and waiting to PVP the bosses
Legs: W/e one helps you, if any

Feet: Explosive Block. This makes boss fights so... so much easier. With PVP mechanics being so prevalent, you nets you a lot more time with the boss on its *** while allowing you to instantly reset him back to kite distance.
Manacles of Force + Dilustel Refractor + Mystic Symbol of the Seven. This gets you max health, max dom, max resto, and max survivability.

Rifle vastly simplifies your job in 9/10 boss fights. The ability to PVP at max range while maintaining your distance is invaluable. It also has the best lunge "duration," allowing you to pre-empt, for example, skull attacks on bosses that often have lungeable skull attacks, completely negating all damage and allowing you to do a second counter before the window closes.

Maximum mitigation and survivability with a single, instant, ranged taunt. The more clippable your loadout, the better. Obviously this will vary from power to power but the goal is to be able to save yourself in those "oh ****" moments. SM is long stretches of boredom followed by near-death moments. If you can, Dash Attack is a good

For most of the climb you can rock offensive trinkets/pets/etc but at a certain point, especially for certain bosses, you should have a 100% pure "I don't want to die, mommy!" setup. For that, I recommend you have an armoury with. Sidekick + Personal Dampening Field + Fiendish Brute's Tome + Heartthrob. Sidekick should be popped whenever available. Personal Dampening Field is a free, clippable, stacking 32k shield. Clipping Heartthrob to Fiendish Brute's Tome nets you an instant, massive health buff, which can be used defensively like an additional shield.

Use Robot Sidekick combined with the Soul Link Affinity. It's exceptionally reliable, gives you an extra 2% mitigation, ups group DPS with no additional effort, gives the bosses something else to target, and can body block.

sections.title: Round 1
items: Feints Lunge into RA (really loves doing this)

Never (or virtually never) does normal lunges without being connected to a feint. If you think he did a normal lunge but you can't tell if he feinted Block into Lunge, don't block until you see the melee combo start or you risk granting immunity

Your lunge reflex instablock game is gonna be strong after having faced a brawler. Turn your muscle memory off and remember not to block the second he lunges because it's always, or almost always, a Feint and he will ruffle your jammies
Has two skull attacks, which he alternates. Random which one he starts on but it doesn't matter because the animations are completely distinct.
Pentathrust Skull attack - very fast such that if you're in range, it's gonna hit you. Will merc non-tanks but pretty safe for the tank
Ye Olde Tusken Dune Raider Skull attack - slams the butt of his spear into the ground then pumps it into the air like you called his mother a bantha. Anyone not blocking will be OHKO'd.

Every now and then he'll look away from the tank, throw his poop at someone, and jump at them. He will often follow this with a lethal (to non-tanks) PBAOE slam attack, a (lethal to non-tanks) frontal spear slam, or his (look if you're a non-tank just assume everything that his you is always gonna kill you in here ok?) Pentathrust skull attack

Best Tactics: Tank: Kite around the outside of the room while PVPing accordingly. Be very careful not to react incorrectly to his feints. He's otherwise pretty harmless. Easiest weapon to tank this fight with is Rifle. If using other weapons, clip your lunges to avoid closing the distance every time you go to PVP him in order to ensure he does as many of his freebie knockdown feints as possible.
Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay spread out at mid to long range. If you ever see him turn and throw his poop, **** immediately.

Survival/Mitigation: People (stupidly) die in this generall by not GTFOing when he throws his poop or by not blocking his Tusken Dune Raider co-splay. Remember to block ever skull until you're sure it's safe. Everyone should keep their soder off CD to pop immediately after Dune Raider goes off, which will hit everyone who's blocking for hefty %-based damage.
Uses Skull attacks less often when continually kited and properly PVPed

sections.title: Round 2
items: 100% incapable of blocking. Can be pre-emptively lunged with impunity. (Seriously, you can trivialize much of this fight if someone other than the tank just spams rifle lunge on him non-stop)
Spams RA hold attack for heavy damage to tank. Will do it 2-4 times back to back.

Does normal lunges followed by melee combos. You can walk away if you're moving when he lunges but the comboes track well and have a good range, so can be hard to pull off reliably Usually safe to roll but if you're not quick you'll eat the tail end of tap-tap-tap-hold.
Fundamentally the same as Underworld Trials minotaur without the adds.
Will occassionally throw beefy, slow-moving axes that deal heavy damage. Avoid them
Will summon orange spinning weapons around the room that follow a specific player. Avoid it and don't drag it onto other people.
Skull attack - aims at a player and charges them. Tracking stops when he starts running

Summons holographic chains on the cardinal directions of the room (a chain spawns every other charge). Group has to get him to break the chain with his charge. Failure to break the chain results in increasingly negative consequences in the form of more and more deadly and aggressive behaviour from the minotaur with each successive miss.
Will occasionally do a soft "lunge" that does low damage but causes a large knockback/stun effect and is generally followed by more deadly attacks on w/o it connects with

Best Tactics: Tank: Loosely kite him around the room but try to keep him positioned such that you can get a good charge at chains when they spawn. Most important thing is to stay away and lunge his RAs. Strongly recommend rifle for this fight, as it allows for cleaner pre-lunging while staying at a safe range.
Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay away from minotaur and dodge axes/aoes. Quickly identify and position to break chains.

Survival/Mitigation: The primary danger to the tank is Minotaur's RAs. Tank should maintain low level mitigation while keeping most available to pop whenever minotaur starts his throw spam. During throw spam, healer should be read to keep the tank topped off.

Do not prioritize chains over dodging aoe. The easiest way to wipe this fight is by grouping up at a chain with an aoe tracking someone and everyone getting caught/CC'd in it because they had tunnel vision trying to break the chain. W/e is being tracked, either stay farther out from the wall than your teammates or stay a little offset and, if you're targetted with charge, line it up at the last second. You can afford to miss a few chains but this is the hardest fight to revive people in (minotaur doesn't have a set rotation with grace periods to allow for revival, like the more overall lethal bosses do).
Tanks can be the target of charge. Charge target may not be who it looks like it's going to be (he can swing 45 degrees sometimes before he starts running, it's janky)

When tanking, don't be afraid to use Dash Attack's movement boost to quickly reposition if an AoE is uncomfortably close to you while he's doing his charged ranged attack spam. That's the combination of factors most likely to cause problems in general. While you can simply move and let someone else handle the lunges, just popping Dash trivializes the situation, lets you get clear instantly, and gets you back on point.

sections.title: Round 3
items: PVP wise, easiest enemy to deal with

Sometimes his normal lunges will "bug out" and he'll land short of your block and start doing a combo. You can either walk away to negate it, or roll away (I don't recommend this until it's established he's in a long combo). Can block the combo but it gets riskier at higher levels

Sometimes successfully blocking his normal lunge has a significantly delayed response, wherein the counter won't trigger for ~1s after the lunger is over. Stay blocked until you see him fall on his ***. If he stop blocking, the counter won't trigger.
This is another fight where Explosive Block is outstanding, since he feints into lunge a lot
Once PVP'd Tank often has enough time to grab 3-4 bombs during bomb phase
This is essentially a heavily watered down version of The Threat Below
Will occasionally press a button on his arm and summon a manta bomb at random position, sometimes in the air. You will hear a subtle beep as well. Stay away from these bombs, as they're lethal.

He only has one skull attack: after a very short grace period, he will use his eye beams on a random player. You can either be out of range (seems unreliable, has a large range) or you can be blocking and immediately breakout and start blocking again once the beam hits you. No matter what you do, this attack is buggy and it's going to kill non-tanks most of the time. Be ready with pickups but be mindful of his randomly summoned bombs when going for and accepting res.

Will summon a circle of bombs three times throughout the fight. At least every third bomb needs to be deactivated. Get the critical bombs then clean up the rest as best you can. Tank can help if he can get a counter off.

Best Tactics: Tank: Kite wide around the room and PVP accordingly. Stay at max range. You can be targeted by eye beams so stay vigilant and do the mechanics for them as required (they're less lethal to the tank). If you're using a weapon other than rifle, be extremely careful when lunging that you don't land on a bomb about to go off.

Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay at max range, spread out around the room and keeping out of the tank's kite path. Do your best to not die to eye beams but pucker up cuz you're gonna. Help each other up as quickly and safely as possible.
Survival/Mitigation: Negligible threat to tank but be prepared to hit the "oh ****" buttons if he's caught up blocking a melee combo. Winning this is all about fast, effective revives.
Try to keep a repair bot active on the field (you squishies are worm food in here) but communicate when you're using it so everyone doesn't go at once

sections.title: Round 4
items: Does unpredictable lunges, combos, and RA hold-hold-hold attacks
Usually runs around doing his bs, ignoring the tank, but will occasionally remember he can PftT and use weapon attacks.
His tornado arms attack is interuptable and extremely dangerous to everyone if left unchecked
Adopt a quick and reactive PVP posture when it comes to handling his normal melee and RA weapon combos.

Overall, he rarely blocks so it's a decent tactic to stand in the middle and spam Rifle lunges at him. At the very least, stay in the middle and reactively lunge his tornadoes and BB. You risk granting immunity but you mitigate a huge amount of his most dangerous attacks

Johnny 's main schtick is he'll pop a Skull then teleport to a random target (all pets are included his target list) and do either air punches, spinny-ma-gig, or tornado arms. Tornado arms is the most dangerous as it can down an entire group extremely quickly and it needs to be interrupted immediately.

When he says "Tag... You're Dead," he's being an edgelord but also about to tether three group members together with electricity, drawing them together via constant CC and dealing lethal damage if they get too close

At 75%, 50%, and 25% health remaining, Johnny summons his afterimages around the middle circle of the room plus one afterimage in the exact center. Everyone needs to run to the center and kill the image there, then huddling in fear until the rest explode. (Ill advised alternate tactic that's good to know below)
Best Tactics: Tank: Stay in the middle of the room so you're always in range to lunge immediately. Johnny is "untankable" and you don't even technically need a tank for this fight.
Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay spread around the room. When he skulls, get ready to pre-emptively block and roll, timing it so when he teleports there's no one there for him to pwn.

Survival/Mitigation: His tornado and his Hold-Hold-Hold RA are his most dangerous moves and impossible to predict. Tank and healer have to stay focusses and avoid getting complacent. His RA spam in particular is the attack most likely to drop a tank, but only because he lulls everyone into a false sense of security. Quick response via shields, soders, and priority heals will neuter him.
Keep your pets out at all times. More pets = more targets = safer for you.
This is one of the easiest but also the most annoying fights, with RNG being the biggest risk factor

When tethered, in addition to staying away from everone else, everyone still needs to avoid his other mechanics. This is extremely frustrating because of the way tether CC works but you can still lunge and roll while it's happening. You just have to spam the inputs as fast as you can.

Alternate afterimage method: If you firmly press your junk against the outer wall exactly smack dab in the direct centerpoint between two of his outer afterimages, you will not be hit when they explode. This is useful to know if you somehow can't make it to the center in time, but don't practice this.

sections.title: Round 6
items: Uses normal RA BB, normal Block, and normal Lunge (potentially flowing directly into a melee combo)

Depending on your latency, it can be rewarding (but extremely risky) to roll away following his lunge. Negates all damage from follow-on combo but potential exists he'll clip you with Hold-Hold and gain immunity.
Feints RA into Block. Be cautious, as fill fake the feint sometimes and cancel the block portion. Wait for visual confirmation of block.
If Shark pins a player and starts omnoming them, he can be Lunge countered

On Skull indicator, Shark will face a played and launch himself swimmingly at them. Everyone needs to roll away as if he connects with his target he will pin them and begin omnomnoming them (lungeable). If he doesn't connect, there is an extreme high probability that he will do a (lethal) PBAOE spin attack for massive damage + CC. He can and will target the tank with this attack.
Spawns water spouts that wander the room and must be avoided.
Does conal PBAOE chum barf that follows the tank

Best Tactics: Tank: Kite around the outside of the room while PVPing accordingly. Keep a close eye on his skull attacks, evading accordingly and immediately lunging if someone gets pinned. Maintain max distance. Easiest weapon to tank this fight with is Rifle. If using other weapons, clip your lunges to avoid closing the distance every time you go to PVP him.

Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay at the very edge of max range, circling the room as needed in order to maintain relative position. Avoid whirlpools while keeping a visual lock on Shark, ready to evade his skully omnoms.

Survival/Mitigation: The combination of Water Spouts and Shark's skull shenanigans make the fight seem more chaotic than it is. Maintain situational awareness. Most deaths occur due to people being too close to Shark after his skull charge and eating his PBAOE. Healers, be prepared to dump some life-ness at the meat shield anytime Shark lunges. Tank, keep some of your mitigation nut in reserve to back the squishy up anytime you get lunged; expect to take a lot of damage.
As much as possible, never face shark towards the center. If the tank has to cross paths, do it so he faces outwards so as to avoid hosing the group with chum barf.

sections.title: Round 7
items: Almost all of his skull atacks are lungeable. Times correctly/preemptively, they can all be double-stuffed to keep him on his *** for twice as long
If you see him do a backflip, start lunging him as it's immediately followed by counterable RA (also double-stuffable)
Does Arrow Storm (lungeable but hard to double stuff)
Does rifle's lungeable combat role (will usually CC you and require breakout)
Does normal lunges (just walk/run away when he does this and it cancels his follow-on combo)

Shortly after you start the fight, he will drop a supply drop on himself and do his lethal beam attack. Tank needs to move him about haveway to the center of the room and keep him pointed such that, when he starts turning his beam, the group will be able to safely follow it in a circle around him. (The beam always goes clockwise)

At regular intervals he will activate Ikon Suit, which must be broken by damage. It's a good idea to coordinate an Orbital Strike order, as the Ikon Suit spacing is such that if everyone takes turns dropping a Strike each per Ikon, the first person to go will be ready again just before the fifth Ikon Suit happens.
He mostly just chases the tank around and gets put on his *** like a chump
Best Tactics: Tank: Kite wide around the room and PVP accordingly. Stay at max range to make it harder to for him start melee comboes. Tanking/PVPing this with rifle is easiest.
Troll/Heal/DPS: Don't get too close, don't clump up, and don't fall asleep.

Survival/Mitigation: The most dangerous attacks he has are rifle forward roll and his melee combos. The rifle forward roll can pull off some nasty damage spikes if the tank gets CC'd at an awkward time. If you hear/see the rifle, drop heals/shields
Do not forget about the beam attack at the start of the fight. Do not forget about the beam attack at the start of the fight. Do not forget about the beam attack at the start of the fight.

_ You should be lunging Deathstroke out of everything. Rifle is ideal for tanking him as it lets you start your lunge the moment before the skull disappears & the attack starts and interrupt before any damage is done, followed immediately by another lunge for a second interrupt on the same vulnerability window. You should never be anywhere near him, staying at max range as much as possible.
The only skull attacks he has that aren't counterable are his beam at the beginning and Shock Staff (which he'll only do if someone is too close).

sections.title: Round 8
items: Prefers RA tap-tap-hold zappy-zaps but does do Solar Flame.
Turns and laughs at target then does either green laser or missiles (Root followed by lethal bombardment). There is now a skull indicator for this mechanic.
Tank: Keep Lex at outside of room. Stay at mid-max range, kiting as needed. PVP accordingly. Easiest/safest weapon to tank Lex with is Rifle, but any weapon will work fine.

Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay at the very edge of max range, circling the room as needed in order to maintain position relative to Lex. If Lex turns to anyone and laughs, that person should run out of range immediately to negate the attack. If the attack was going to be bombardment, he'll instead do it at his feet.

Survival/Mitigation: Most damage is mitigated by doing the mechanic cleanly. Expect the tank to take some damage from Solar Flame at higher levels. Maintain a base level of shielding but Tank & Healer should keep a reserve nut for any "oh ****" moments that may pop up.

If you're slow and don't move out of range of the mechanic fast enough, you'll get rooted by Lex' bombardment, you'll have to breakout before you can roll/run away. Sometimes people forget about the rooting component of the attack and die comically, rolling/running in place.

If someone is killed by bombardment, do not attempt to revive them until the green LL logo has disappeared. Despite the missile animation being complete, the (lethal) damage persists until the aoe dissipates.
The green laser will OHKO non-tanks
For tanks, intentionally allowing yourself to become rooted by bombardment is an effective (but risky and unnecessary) means of activating Breakout Protection

sections.title: Round 9
items: Spaaaaaaaaaaaams mortar for hella damage. Needs to be lunged every time.
Lunges (does neglible damage and you can/should just walk away from it)
Occasionally summons a green shield that needs to be broken by DPS or he heals (it goes down easily)

Occasionally points his Pez Dispenser in the air and launches an umbrella of baby blue Pez around the room. Keep an eye out for the bright blue spots on the ground so you're not near them when they explode.

Skull attack is dependent on proximity. If no one is anywhere near him, he will always do flamethrower. If anyone is too close, he might instead do an extremely dangerous lighting attack that hits everyone, regardless of where they are in the room.
Occasionally summons easy-to-spot and avoid bombs around the room. Most dangerous to the tank.

Best Tactics: Tank: DO NOT USE RIFLE FOR THIS FIGHT. USE ANY WEAPON BESIDES RIFLE. If use rifle, it's quasi-stationary lunge means you eat full damage from at least one and often two volleys of Mortar every time he does it. This is extremely hard to deal with at round 19 and completely untenable at 29. It's important you use a weapon with a full lunge range so that you're both countering Mortar and evading most of its damage. Do not clip cancel your lunge until you are safely outside of Mortar's AoE. Kite him around the room, with the following priorities: #1 - If he Mortarts, lunge him and immediately **** as far away as possible while remaining within lunge range. #2 - Kite at max range at all times but avoid moving into the grey. If you're too far, your lunge will fail to counter Mortar. #3 - Anytime he lunges you, **** to max range immediately. The most dangerous possible situation to be in in this is US lunging then immediately doing a skull attack, as he's close enough it could be his lightning blast. Done correctly, you can do this entire fight without a single lightning blast. While kiting, be careful of bombs that may be ahead of your kite path (you won't see them until they're close since your camera should be locked on US), close to US (such that you may land in them when you lunge), or in the lunge path to US. At higher levels, be extremely diligent about avoiding his baby blue Pez on the ground. It won't kill you by itself but Pez Asplosion + Mortar can.

Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay at 100% max range at all times. Being ultra-vigilent about dodging his Pez on the ground, as it can OHKO you. When he skulls, always block and stay blocked until you're 100% certain he's doing fire and not lightning. Fire begins with the barrel of his rifle pointing about 5-10 degrees up abruptly without him moving much otherwise. Lightning begins with him swinging his whole body dramatically and dropping his left elbow for the world's most epic fist pump. If you're not blocking and he does lightning, you're probably dead. If it's fire and he's pointing it at you (which... WHY ARE YOU IN RANGE TO BE FLAMETHROWERED?! STEVE!?) you have to away roll immediately and keep rolling until you're out of range or you're probably dead (the fire is sometimes invisible)/

Survival/Mitigation: You survive this respecting this angry vet's his personal space. Stay far away and if you do get even mid-range for any reason whatsoever, take a sec and go back to max range. You will only lose this by not respecting his personal space.
Done correctly, this one of the easiest fights. Done incorrectly, it's the hardest.

sections.title: 20-30 Bosses' Key Points (preliminary season 1 tips)
items: Lex Luthor - Handle same as previous iterations but tank needs to be on top of pre-empting Solar Flame (not in one-shot territory yet but getting there)

King Shark - Tank needs to pre-empt PVPing Stomp Smashes, keeping in mind he'll spam it several times in a row. The biggest challenge here is just getting used to King Shark's use of brawling, which differs slightly from Ultraman who you're still going to have muscle memory for from 20. KS leaves more time for roll-out but also requires different Phase Dodge timing. His Chum Barf(TM) is now lethal to tanks after ~1s. As tank, do not attempt to block break him... his feint brackets often bug out and even when they don't the room's mechanics severely occlude them and make it so attempting to block break is the riskiest thing you can do. If you see him block, you block until you're 100% sure he's actually just blocking and not feinting a lunge (this is best practice in general in SM, as the feints are buggy).
Vandal Savage - The only difference here is that his Pokey Stabs(TM) Skull attack should now be avoided, as it's moderately lethal and the dot it applies is pretty potent now

Johnny Quick - Same squishy **** he's always been but his tornado attacks are a lot more lethal. Also, if you let him get off an uninterrupted MA ranged combo it can wipe anyone in a ~90degree arc where he's facing. More important than ever for the group form a triangle around the room with the tank in the center, lunging his BS w/e needed.

Black Manta - Same as always but his melee combo finishers are now unliveable. Tank should kite/pvp like usual, using roll/PD to mitigate his melee bs and Amazonian Deflection to deal with eye beams (I didn't use it but I suspect Man-Bat form would make escaping his melee significantly easier). Explosive Block is more valuable here than anywhere and helps land Orbital Strikes more reliably but when you see him feinting into lunge, take a few steps back towards him (his lunge range is slightly dwarfed and if you're at or near max range there will be a semi-dangerous delay before the block actually procs and bounces him). If the tank does go down, do not attempt to revive if Black Manta is near the corpse or there's a solid chance he'll Fart Jump(TM) away and kill you.
Deathstroke - Same as always but his bullet spray is now extremely dangerous. Other than that, PVP like normal and pre-empt his bs.

Minotaur - PVP like normal and pre-empt his bs. His melee combo is still livable but you're better off just eating the tap tap tap part then popping PD for the HOLD (choppity chop) part then immediately blocking near the end of the animation to try and get a free bounce proc. As long as everyone communicates where the whirling hammers are and the hammer target kites it appropriately, this is pretty straightforward. Tank should keep Dash Attack in reserve for either getting out of risky-looking situations where there's a hammer closing in or Dash should also be popped if there's a chain up and the charge targets the tank, as Dash will allow you to quickly spin him to face the chain. The more people who pop henchmen during/immediately after the charge the better, as they'll encircle him while he's staggered and bodyblock him against the wall for their full duration if done correctly.

Ultimate Soldier - Mortars are now extremely lethal. You need to either roll away or lunge him when you see the white mortar shells at about the height of your head. Too soon or too late and you'll take full damage. Phase Dodge should be kept in reserve and Amazonian Deflection can be used to ignore mortars. He'll occasionally enter a mortar spam phase where he'll keep taking a few steps forward then mortaring over and over until he's PVPed; this is dangerous because he can really cut into the middle of the room if he's not put on his *** in a timely fashion. Expect this fight to take ~25-30min, therefore expect server lag bs to result in several seconds of weird behaviour at some point during every attempt (I actually do encourage the use of Man-Bat form for 29, simply to mitigate the fact that lag can/will result in bs Arcs w/o it while running from his lunges). Everyone who can should use Grimorium Verum and as many pets as possible in general, as it makes him stop and flame the air way more often. Initial guide used by courtesy of Crash Allen'

sections.title: Overview
items: Titan’s Training Sim is a Survival Mode 2.0 instance taking place in the Titans Tower.
Progress points are given after every two rounds and after round 10 the adds and bosses appear again, but with higher CR.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: The Teen Titans are looking for the best of the best to run their new Advanced Holographic Technology through its paces. Think you've got what it takes?

sections.title: General Tips
items: It's a marathon, not a sprint. More DPS = shorter fights = less time for mistakes to happen, but max DPS doesn't equate to cleanest/safest. I've found a balanced approach is best.

You don't need to be some meta DW flurry spam group to do well. SM is all "about passing the exam," ie. knowing the mechanics and doing them. The better you do the mechanics, the easier your life is to the point you can completely trivialize most of the bosses. Mechanics come first, always.

The DPS doesn't need to be max CR/SP as long as they're good at the mechanics and can do good damage regardless. The supports, especially the tank, should be, as you really want the toughest shields you can get your hands on. That said, the tank is the most important and beyond that there's a lot more flexibility. Don't think you can't do SM if you aren't maxed out yet.
Robot Sidekick (and pets in general) is your best friend in here
Manacles of Force is worth thoughtful consideration

Additional tip that virtually everyone has overlooked: Lazarus Pit Water is OP af in SM, especially in the longer, higher rounds where it's basically up as often as you need it to be and it has the potential to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat where you'd otherwise lose 40+ minutes of work. With the potential exception of DPS vs Vampire Lord (due to the soft DPS checks on his shadow pets), the more people who can run it the better. I keep it in my primary boss loadouts then have backup "He is Risen" loadouts that I quick swap to to replace Lazarus w w/e artifact I want. Don't just insta-pop it though; do revives like normal with Water as a last resort, to be popped at the last second if it's in doubt that someone can reach the cog in time. Even if you know you're going to die as soon as you get up, you'll still get another 10s window where hopefully a teammate can revive you.

sections.title: Tank Build
items: Tank is the most critical role in SM and, in addition to knowing the bossfights to a tee, you should be built to maximize your chances of success. Since that's heavily PVP dependent with no sustained blocking and no adds (that you're ultimately responsible for) outside of trash waves, that means your tank build's gonna be a lot different.
Head: If you're Super Speed, and using it, Energized Dash Attack is ideal. Otherwise this is player's choice.

Neck: Fortified Assault, with extra in your inventory in case you want to switch to Fortified Blocking for Ultraman (if his lunge combos are messing you up more than his ranged attacks). Overall, Fortified Assault is BiS in SM since we spend most of our time kiting and waiting to PVP the bosses
Legs: W/e one helps you, if any

Feet: Explosive Block. This makes boss fights so... so much easier. With PVP mechanics being so prevalent, you nets you a lot more time with the boss on its *** while allowing you to instantly reset him back to kite distance.
Manacles of Force + Dilustel Refractor + Mystic Symbol of the Seven. This gets you max health, max dom, max resto, and max survivability.

Rifle vastly simplifies your job in 9/10 boss fights. The ability to PVP at max range while maintaining your distance is invaluable. It also has the best lunge "duration," allowing you to pre-empt, for example, skull attacks on bosses that often have lungeable skull attacks, completely negating all damage and allowing you to do a second counter before the window closes.

Maximum mitigation and survivability with a single, instant, ranged taunt. The more clippable your loadout, the better. Obviously this will vary from power to power but the goal is to be able to save yourself in those "oh ****" moments. SM is long stretches of boredom followed by near-death moments. If you can, Dash Attack is a good

For most of the climb you can rock offensive trinkets/pets/etc but at a certain point, especially for certain bosses, you should have a 100% pure "I don't want to die, mommy!" setup. For that, I recommend you have an armoury with. Sidekick + Personal Dampening Field + Fiendish Brute's Tome + Heartthrob. Sidekick should be popped whenever available. Personal Dampening Field is a free, clippable, stacking 32k shield. Clipping Heartthrob to Fiendish Brute's Tome nets you an instant, massive health buff, which can be used defensively like an additional shield.

Use Robot Sidekick combined with the Soul Link Affinity. It's exceptionally reliable, gives you an extra 2% mitigation, ups group DPS with no additional effort, gives the bosses something else to target, and can body block.

sections.title: Round 1
items: Feints Lunge into RA (really loves doing this)

Never (or virtually never) does normal lunges without being connected to a feint. If you think he did a normal lunge but you can't tell if he feinted Block into Lunge, don't block until you see the melee combo start or you risk granting immunity

Your lunge reflex instablock game is gonna be strong after having faced a brawler. Turn your muscle memory off and remember not to block the second he lunges because it's always, or almost always, a Feint and he will ruffle your jammies
Has two skull attacks, which he alternates. Random which one he starts on but it doesn't matter because the animations are completely distinct.
Pentathrust Skull attack - very fast such that if you're in range, it's gonna hit you. Will merc non-tanks but pretty safe for the tank
Ye Olde Tusken Dune Raider Skull attack - slams the butt of his spear into the ground then pumps it into the air like you called his mother a bantha. Anyone not blocking will be OHKO'd.

Every now and then he'll look away from the tank, throw his poop at someone, and jump at them. He will often follow this with a lethal (to non-tanks) PBAOE slam attack, a (lethal to non-tanks) frontal spear slam, or his (look if you're a non-tank just assume everything that his you is always gonna kill you in here ok?) Pentathrust skull attack

Best Tactics: Tank: Kite around the outside of the room while PVPing accordingly. Be very careful not to react incorrectly to his feints. He's otherwise pretty harmless. Easiest weapon to tank this fight with is Rifle. If using other weapons, clip your lunges to avoid closing the distance every time you go to PVP him in order to ensure he does as many of his freebie knockdown feints as possible.
Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay spread out at mid to long range. If you ever see him turn and throw his poop, **** immediately.

Survival/Mitigation: People (stupidly) die in this generall by not GTFOing when he throws his poop or by not blocking his Tusken Dune Raider co-splay. Remember to block ever skull until you're sure it's safe. Everyone should keep their soder off CD to pop immediately after Dune Raider goes off, which will hit everyone who's blocking for hefty %-based damage.
Uses Skull attacks less often when continually kited and properly PVPed

The only skull attacks he has that aren't counterable are his beam at the beginning and Shock Staff (which he'll only do if someone is too close).

sections.title: Round 7
items: 100% incapable of blocking. Can be pre-emptively lunged with impunity. (Seriously, you can trivialize much of this fight if someone other than the tank just spams rifle lunge on him non-stop)
Spams RA hold attack for heavy damage to tank. Will do it 2-4 times back to back.

Does normal lunges followed by melee combos. You can walk away if you're moving when he lunges but the comboes track well and have a good range, so can be hard to pull off reliably Usually safe to roll but if you're not quick you'll eat the tail end of tap-tap-tap-hold.
Fundamentally the same as Underworld Trials minotaur without the adds.
Will occassionally throw beefy, slow-moving axes that deal heavy damage. Avoid them
Will summon orange spinning weapons around the room that follow a specific player. Avoid it and don't drag it onto other people.
Skull attack - aims at a player and charges them. Tracking stops when he starts running

Summons holographic chains on the cardinal directions of the room (a chain spawns every other charge). Group has to get him to break the chain with his charge. Failure to break the chain results in increasingly negative consequences in the form of more and more deadly and aggressive behaviour from the minotaur with each successive miss.
Will occasionally do a soft "lunge" that does low damage but causes a large knockback/stun effect and is generally followed by more deadly attacks on w/o it connects with

Best Tactics: Tank: Loosely kite him around the room but try to keep him positioned such that you can get a good charge at chains when they spawn. Most important thing is to stay away and lunge his RAs. Strongly recommend rifle for this fight, as it allows for cleaner pre-lunging while staying at a safe range.
Troll/Heal/DPS: Stay away from minotaur and dodge axes/aoes. Quickly identify and position to break chains.

Survival/Mitigation: The primary danger to the tank is Minotaur's RAs. Tank should maintain low level mitigation while keeping most available to pop whenever minotaur starts his throw spam. During throw spam, healer should be read to keep the tank topped off.

Do not prioritize chains over dodging aoe. The easiest way to wipe this fight is by grouping up at a chain with an aoe tracking someone and everyone getting caught/CC'd in it because they had tunnel vision trying to break the chain. W/e is being tracked, either stay farther out from the wall than your teammates or stay a little offset and, if you're targetted with charge, line it up at the last second. You can afford to miss a few chains but this is the hardest fight to revive people in (minotaur doesn't have a set rotation with grace periods to allow for revival, like the more overall lethal bosses do).
Tanks can be the target of charge. Charge target may not be who it looks like it's going to be (he can swing 45 degrees sometimes before he starts running, it's janky)

When tanking, don't be afraid to use Dash Attack's movement boost to quickly reposition if an AoE is uncomfortably close to you while he's doing his charged ranged attack spam. That's the combination of factors most likely to cause problems in general. While you can simply move and let someone else handle the lunges, just popping Dash trivializes the situation, lets you get clear instantly, and gets you back on point.

title: Survival Mode: Fortress of Solitude
summary: The Fortress of Solitude is a Survival Mode instance with a large arena where positioning is much more relaxed as in tighter spots. Players generally should form circles or semi-circles around bosses and use the space for their advantage.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Fortress of Solitude is a Survival Mode instance with a large arena where positioning is much more relaxed as in tighter spots. Players generally should form circles or semi-circles around bosses and use the space for their advantage.
After round 10 the adds and bosses appear again, but with higher CR and merely one progress point after round 15.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: Think you've got what it takes to stop Brainiac's mind controlled Super Heroes and Villains? Queue up and see how long you can last against unending waves of powerful enemies!

sections.title: Possible Adds
items: The Alpha Triads come in groups of three. Their special attack is to pull players in. This should be countered by an immediate rolling away.
The Sunstone Assassin will put a large ground tag on a player before his special attack. The tagged player as well as all players near him have to block.

The Sunstone Golem shoots large fire balls in all directions, which will explode after a while. Players should stay away from the moment they see that, some can be also avoided, but getting to max range is safer.
Another of his skulls attacks is a "Doom Spin" type of attack which is deadly for everyone including the tanks. Try to keep your keep distance and crowd control him.

Every once in a while the Sunstone Phaser will become untargetable and then release several huge AOE pulses ended by one fatal final blow. Every player including the tank(s) should move out the AOE's radius.

sections.title: Round 1
items: Encasement with tail that must break out as soon as possible.
Laser beam with tail or arms that can be blocked otherwise he'll 1 shot , it roots and grounds. This attack is manly done after encasing the tank, or another person.

He goes underground and he will make ice balls fall from the ceiling, Must be avoided by moving from initial position or blocked ( wtih fortified blocking) Before doing this attack he will move his legs up and hold them in the air for a bit.
When underground he'll pick one person and follow him up, must move around, he'll get out of the Ice from time to time and jump to that person. It can be a pet as well.
When he's underground is simply better to stay out of his range.
He can shake his tail really fast doing an AOE attack from his tail, it will be small pieces of ice that can bounce around, Doge or block.
Melee attack with his arms and tail usually directed to the tank, and Melee ground pounds.
Small range lasers from his arms that usually are directed to the tank.
Tank should stay at close range from the scorpion. (Needs further testing but aparently drops aggro on long range to the tank)
Beam that can lift you up. It should be broken out and block until animation is gone. (It must be tested further to see if its randomly or has a mechanic itself)
Ice ball attack looks like pop-corn, more often just after the laser beam attack. Can be doged or blocked

sections.title: Round 2
items: Skull Attack: Charge Spin (Must be avoided or blocked by tank)
Thruster attack (Attack with his feet, must be out of range when he does that attack)
Hand blaster type Pulse Beam (Take his arms behind and then back to the front, must be blocked)
Brawling "Tap range" Must be blocked or avoided (Probably done to the furthest of the group)
Brawling melee combos (vulnerables to block) This attack only hits usually tank.
Laser beam (Probably to the furtherst of the group, must be blocked or 1 shot) Usually this attack comes after the Brawling tap range, or the pulse beam.
Hand blaster Power discharge (flamethrower type) Usually directed do the tank, but it's a cone AOE, that could potentialy kill people at close range.

Supercharge: (Super-Nova attack) : Really big pulse type AoE that 1 shots, same type like Carol Ferris special attack.(Hands goes back in a "Grow strong" kind of pose, Leaning back and lifting his arms). Must be out of range or block to survive the attack.
He does a pull with the same type of motion as the pulse beam attack. Either you block it to not be pulled or the tank uses the group break out.
Below 35% he'll do a "Spontaneous Combustion" from fire power type of attack, mid ranged. And will start doing his attack in faster intervals.
Skull attacks: Charge that might end up pounding the floor into an AOE, or making ice balls fall from the ceeling. Goes to furthest person in the group.
High jumps are type of lunge that can be countered with a block.
Mostly melee attacks, with a few exception that can be block breaks to the tank.

sections.title: Round 3
items: Mostly brawling type of attacks. Included a block breaking, Brawling Hold Range type of attack.
Skull attacks : There are two skull attacks. Usually the second one willfollow in a short period of time after the first was used.
1 - Crystal Snow Ball throws in a Cone AoE type of attack. This can be avoided or blocked.
2 - Ground pound AoE, that will let Crystal shards go in an AoE, that should be blocked or avoided.
The group should be standing at max range to avoid this attacks.
Ground pounds, and hand attacks just like the Burden of Crête in the Spike Room in Labyrinth, that also push you.

He'll do a pull lifting his arms backwards, and his head looking up, followed by a ground pound, that if you're not at a safe distance he will be able to pull you and kill you. If this happens to kill someone one should wait before going to save a team-mate or you'll get killed in the second AoE ground pound.
"Meteor Blast" Type of animation attack. This attack will be shoot from his arm and it must be avoided or blocked.

There is a moment when he'll do a small pause and he'll lift his arms up, if you're blocking this attack can block break you. This attack is vulnerable to interrupt, so it must be lunged, or use an immunity so the block break doesnt take effect.
The attack has the same type of animation as the Meteor Blast.
It has a delay with the animation just like carol ferris tentacles in Love and War, one must wait a bit before lunging.
This attack is often followed by the Meteor Blast attack mentioned above.

sections.title: Round 4
items: Mostly Martial Arts weapon attacks. He has also ranged martial arts attack that block breaks and can be lethal to the tank. It's vulnerable to interrupt.

AoE Pull centered in him, he'll do the "grow strong" animation from the emotes. It is vulnerable to interrupt by a lunge. Group break outs are really usefull so team mates doesnt get pulled by him. That pull will heal him as well so it's usefull to have a heal debuff on him.
Two handed weapon attacks, the Horizontal hold range hammer throw will block break, and it's vulnerable to interrupt.
With his hammer he'll do tap range attack from the staff weapon tree. Usually a skull attack comes after performing this attack in particular.

Vertical Hammer Throw with purple colored effects on it. (Probably to the furthest away in the group, needs more testing) He'll face someone in the group, then it will throw it. It can be doged if timed right. This throw does damage in a small cone, around 15-20 degrees.

Charge that is a 1 shot, it must be blocked to survive. This charge is performed with the hammer, and will do a small AoE damage around the person who is targeter. It can be body blocked in order to change the path of the charge.
Hammer attack with a blue pulse, that damages in AoE around the Tank. The animation is the same as 5 tap melee with Two handed.
Important to note: Steel also drops Mines around where he is, those mines can be really dangerous and must be avoided by the group.

sections.title: Round 5
items: He has one attack where he does a ground pound that has a huge AoE and usually 1 shots people who aren't blocking. This attack has no real tell for it as such but there is a way to tell when it's coming.
This fight is very much about doing damage in intervals and blocking.

Non will point in a direction and charge in that general direction. When he points the group has to block and stay blocked, this is important, because after charging he will do one other action. Often this will be a lunge at the tank or charge at another person, sometimes he'll do something else like freeze breath or heat vision but no matter what he does he will ALWAYS use that ground pound that will 1 shot people.

So the best way to avoid people getting KO'd is for the tank to call out when Non points and have the group block until he uses his ground pound. It is important that everyone stays blocked except healers and/or trolls who can use a power quickly and go back into blocking.

Knowing when to attack and when to block is the key to this fight! Second thing is that you absolutely shouldn't rush to revive people when they get KO'd because Non might use his 1 shot, so make sure to keep track on whether Non charged recently or not before going for the revive.

sections.title: Round 9
items: Controlled Krypto has two abilities that are unbreakable stuns if you don't block it. First one is basically like freeze breath, if you aren't blocking through it you'll be stuck in a shivering animation until it ends. The other is like a takedown where he pins you to the ground until he's done you, like the previous one, you don't get stunned if you are blocking. Both attacks start of with a couple of smaller ticks followed by a big one.
He also charges at the group members but seemingly he doesn't really go for anyone else but the tank if the group is focusing down the other boss first.

sections.title: General Tips
items: If the bosses are tanked on opposite sides of the arena, one healer needs to stay in healing range of the tank not with the group.

title: Tales of Kennik
summary: Tales of Kennik is a story blog released on January 2026 on the game's website.

sections.title: Overview
items: Tales of Kennik is a story blog released on January 2026 on the game's website.
It serves as part of the prelude to Hope Burns Bright.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: What starts as a child's hopeful journal quickly becomes a chilling account of fear, loss, and unanswered questions on a graying Mogo. Follow these deeply personal entries as rumors grow, trust erodes, and survival depends on finding the truth behind the Red Lanterns' promises.

sections.title: Summary
items: In the form of a diary of Kennik, a non-human child on Mogo, it consists of five entries.
Entry One - Having traded berries for a Thoughtscriber for journaling, Kennik marvels at the many alien cultures they learn about from kids from other planets.
Entry Two - Weather becomes cold as Mogo goes gray. The elders want to move south, but the lanterns are preoccupied with Nekron's forces.
Entry Three - The refugees grow suspicious of the intentions of Red Lanterns herding them.
Entry Four - Kennik contemplates escaping with others.
Entry Five - Another child overheard that the Red Lanterns are taking the children to another, safer place. The adults consider resisting the Reds, and Kennik fears the worst.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This story blog features interior artwork from Red Lanterns #16 (2013) by Andres Guinaldo, and from Red Lanterns #26 (2014) by Jim Calafiore. It also features an early screenshot of a refugee camp on Frozen Mogo.

In Light and Rain chronology:; Entry One takes place shortly before the events of Fearful Day.; Entry Two takes place concurrently with the events of Raging Night.; Entries Three, Four, and Five take place somewhat before the events of Hope Burns Bright.
Kennik's journal continues in A Child's Journey (Investigations).

The planet Hul-Hollix seems to be original to the game. Since Kennik's race is undisclosed and his appearance does not seem to match any other race in the comics, it is possible that Hul-Hollix is his home planet.

sections.title: Story
items: It's the season of love and the Olympian goddess Aphrodite has staged a battle to see whether Circe-like Scorn or Wonder Woman-like Devotion will rule the human hearts in the months to come. Choose your side and triumph in the name of love.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: The Temple of Aphrodite is a level 30 event, part of the Valentine's Day Event. The alert consists of a single symmetrical arena, with the aspects of Scorn and Devotion battling for dominance. Starting out, the players must choose which side they will be fighting for. This choice is there for feat purposes and has no impact on gameplay. After a side is chosen, talk to Aphrodite to begin the alert.

sections.title: Objective
items: To complete the event, players must carry the enemy side's Hearts to their fountain to convert them. The enemies themselves consist of constantly spawning imps or cherubs that will attempt to convert the players' side Hearts. The objective is to gain a significant lead of approximately 20 Hearts. Progress can be tracked via the aspects' fight in the middle.

sections.title: Transforming
items: Players may use their fountain to transform into an Imp or Cherub. While in this form they are given flight, a bow with limited combos and 3 abilities:
Consume Heart - consumes all nearby floating purple hearts. This provides a flight speed boost and 10% Supercharge
Heart Nova - instantly kills all enemies in a small AoE, 25% Supercharge cost. Note: transforming drains the Supercharge meter
The transformation isn't required to defeat the alert.

sections.title: Rewards
items: Players may receive loot once per day.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This was the only in-game appearance of Aphrodite as an NPC.

title: Test Server
summary: The Test Server is accessible via an extra PC client - and thus an extra DCUO installation - and is used by the developers to make changes in the game available for (beta) testing.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Test Server is accessible via an extra PC client - and thus an extra DCUO installation - and is used by the developers to make changes in the game available for (beta) testing.

Using the test server was originally only possible for members and nowadays for all those interested. Characters built on it are not transferable to the live servers, but will stay on the test server beyond content updates until deleted by the player. Gear, artifact XP and currency are provided by special vendors in order for players not having to worry about leveling up their created characters.

Usually game updates and new episodes are put on the test server for a while prior to their official release for players to test the new features and give feedback on the Testing Feedback board in the official DCUO Forums.
As of 2026 the test server client can be downloaded at http://launch.daybreakgames.com/installer/DCUO_Test_setup.exe.

sections.title: Notes
items: On occasion of the Stats Revamp (2017) the test server was completely reset and all player characters and leagues previously created were deleted in the process.

As of 2023 the test server has periods of unavailability (offline) and/or unaccessibility (no login possible). Apart from the daily server reset (~30 mins) this usually happens before new content (episodes) is about to be released and likely indicates an internal testing phase by the developers.
Whether the test server is up and running can be determined on the Game Server Status page.
As of March 2025 the test server has been unavailable for regular users since before christmas 2024 and it is not clear if it is coming back.

sections.title: Background
items: Little is known about the French scientist and criminal genius known as the Brain. Before his death, the scientist experimented on a captured African gorilla and gave it a near-genius intellect. When the scientist died, the ape, named Monsieur Mallah, removed the man's brain and put it in a receptacle connected to a vast computer network. The scientist, now called the Brain, set up the villainous Brotherhood of Evil to further his goal of world conquest.

sections.title: Involvement
items: The Brain, along with Monsieur Mallah, is an iconic villain who appears at various locations in Metropolis as part of the More Than You Can Chew and Fanboy feats. If a hero encounters him he will knock them back and then leave, if a villain encounters him he will make a comment and then disappear.

title: The Game's Afoot
summary: The Game's Afoot is a story blog released on January 2025 on the game's website.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Game's Afoot is a story blog released on January 2025 on the game's website.
It serves as part of the prelude to Day of Reckoning.

sections.title: Summary
items: Detective Chimp has a meeting with John Constantine in the Oblivion Bar. Chimp is concerned about the new killing spreed in Gotham City, as the mysterious Exobyte Killer seem to now be targeting magic users, and asks Constantine to investigate one of the crime scenes.

Constantine arrives at an alleyway near 22 Haney Avenue by Gotham City waterfront. He notices signs of fight between superpowered individuals, and a spell tells him that the victim was disintegrated. Batman appears and the two exchange notes. The Bat notes that the killer has only recently turned to magic users, and the nightly murders has stopped for 72 hours — which means that the killer might've left the city, so he has told Superman to keep an eye for the killer in Metropolis. He tells Constantine to ask Zatanna to contact him if he finds anything new, and the two part ways.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This story blog features interior artwork from Day of Vengeance #1 (2005) by Justiniano, and from Injustice: Gods Among Us: Year Three #1 and Injustice: Gods Among Us: Year Three #2 (2014) by Bruno Redondo.

Haney Avenue doesn't exist in the game nor in the comics. It's most likely named after Bob Haney, one of the creators of the Doom Patrol and the original Teen Titans. The warehouse at 22 Haney Avenue doesn't match any building in Gotham City or Tricorner.
This is the first time the wizard Wotan is mentioned in the game's lore. He was created by Gardner Fox and Howard Sherman as a foe to Doctor Fate, first appearing in More Fun Comics #55 (1940).
"The game is afoot" is a quote popularly associated with Sherlock Holmes.

title: The Hunt for Kryb
summary: The Hunt for Kryb is a story blog released on May 2026 on the game's website.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Hunt for Kryb is a story blog released on May 2026 on the game's website.
It serves as part of the prelude to Shadows Over Argo, following the events of Hope Burns Bright's Mother Knows Best epilogue.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: She crossed sectors. Called in favors. And the trail's still cold. Things are just getting started...

sections.title: Summary
items: Supergirl is called to meet up with Guy Gardner at Mogo's sector. Guy reveals Kryb survived and is experimenting with Kryptonian Tech. However, not even Lobo could track her down. They visit Thanagar but Hawkman and Hawkgirl do not have info either, nor do Mister Miracle or Big Barda when they are contacted. Finally, when Guy is called back to Oa, the Atom suggests Supergirl to meet up with Luzia and bring Krypto to hopefully find Kryb.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This story blog features interior artwork from Krypto: The Last Dog of Krypton #1 (2025) by Mike Norton, Lobo Unbound #2 (2003) by Alex Horley, Hawkman Vol 4 #1 (2002) by Rags Morales, and Supergirl Vol 7 #24 (2019) by Evan Shaner. It also features art from the variant cover for Supergirl Vol 7 #2 (2016) by Bengal.

This story blog seem to imply (though not directly affirm) that; Czarnia is located on Sector 2010. The sector of Lobo's planet is never specified in the comics, and neither is what lies in sector 2010.; Apokolips is located on Sector 38. This is taken from an outdated version of the planet from the Pre-Flashpoint continuity, before the concept of the God Sphere was created. In the game, Apokolips and New Genesis were already established as part of the Sphere (as seen in Fractured God Sphere and The Terrorium), which is a metaphysical reality separated from the Infinite Earths populated by the gods that are and the gods that were.

title: The Predator
summary: The Predator is the emotional entity of the Star Sapphire Corps.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Predator is the emotional entity of the Star Sapphire Corps.

sections.title: Background
items: It was originally believed to merely be a side-effect of Carol Ferris using the Star Sapphire gem.

The Predator, however, is in fact the ultimate embodiment of love - love with nothing to temper it. The love entity has inhabited several hosts over the last millennium, most notably the Earth-woman Carol Ferris. The entity emphasizes the aggressive nature in one's being, making the subject paranoid and highly obsessive. The Predator imbues its host with the power to latch onto and manipulate people's minds, and is able to change and affect them at the host's will.

sections.title: Involvement
items: In the War of the Light Part II raid Love and War, The Predator aids Carol Ferris in her fight against the players, Sinestro, and Hal Jordan.
In the Episode 15 duo Corrupted Zamaron, players must cleanse Zamaron and The Predator of Nekron's corruption.

title: The Right Guy
summary: The Right Guy is a story blog released on January 2026 on the game's website.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Right Guy is a story blog released on January 2026 on the game's website.
It serves as part of the prelude to Hope Burns Bright. The story continues with the chapter mission Refugees' Lament: Search for Survivors.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: The Right Guy follows Guy Gardner and Saint Walker as they balance rebuilding, rescue, and the weight of impossible choices in the wake of galaxy-shaking conflict. As refugees seek warmth and shelter, deeper questions loom about redemption, rage, and whether everyone can truly be saved. With humor, heart, and tension, this chapter asks who's really the right guy when hope alone may not be enough.

sections.title: Summary
items: The Lanterns (represented by Carol Ferris, John Stewart, Atrocitus, Sinestro, and Brother Warth, amongst others) hold a meeting to decide how they are going to approach the Sorrow crisis. Meanwhile, Guy Gardner muses about the villain Evil Star to Saint Walker while preparing a refugee camp. The duo discusses the situation on Mogo and how to deal with Luzia Cavalera. Guy believes Luzia is beyond redemption, while Walker has hope that she can be restored — but both share suspicion about the Red Lantern Corps volunteering to help with evacuating the refugees.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This story blog is the first to not feature any artwork.

items: The Right One For The Job is a story blog released on May 2025 on the game's website.
It serves as part of the prelude to Fearful Day. The story continues in the chapter mission Battle for Mogo: Reinforce the Frontline.

sections.title: Summary
items: Luzia Cavalera goes to The Atom for help in checking on her sister Esperanza. He contacts the Watchtower and Booster Gold informs him that Guy Gardner is the only Green Lantern on Earth at the moment.
Luzia finds Guy in Baltimore and they stop the Royal Flush Gang from robbing a bank; Guy cannot leave Earth but gives her directions to Mogo.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This story blog features interior artwork from The Atom #26 (1966) by Gil Kane, and Green Lantern Vol 7 #10 (2024) by Evan Shaner.
First mention of Royal Flush Gang, which has never appeared in the game.

The Atom mentions Ted Kord to Booster Gold but, according to the Watchtower Containment Facility briefings, the second Blue Beetle is dead - as the early game shares most of its continuity with the Pre-Flashpoint era, he was presumably killed by Maxwell Lord during the events leading to Infinite Crisis. In the comics, after the events of DCU: Rebirth (2016), his story was rewritten - he had now retired from the field due to cardiac issues. His new background was added to the game's lore as part of the developers initiative to make it more similar to current DC Comics continuity, but no explanation was given to his in-game resurrection.

title: Toyman (Winslow Schott)
summary: The Toyman is Winslow P. Schott, a genius inventor and criminal mastermind who uses crafted toy-based or toy-themed devices and gimmicks to aid in his various crimes.

sections.title: Overview
items: The Toyman is Winslow P. Schott, a genius inventor and criminal mastermind who uses crafted toy-based or toy-themed devices and gimmicks to aid in his various crimes.

sections.title: Background
items: Winslow P. Schott was only a small boy when he made his first toy, a balsa-wood airplane painted blue and red. Another boy stole the plane, an act that had a profound effect on Winslow and may have ultimately driven him to use toys to rob others. When he grew up, Schott created some of the most amazing toys ever conceived, for which he received widepread acclaim. However, LexCorp's acquisition of Schott's toy company left him jobless and burning for revenge against LexCorp's owner, Lex Luthor.
Schott's failed attempts to kill Luthor with various lethal toys eventually led to an association with Intergang and a criminal career as the Toyman, becoming an adversary of Superman.

sections.title: Alternate Future
items: In the alternate future, Schott was killed alongside the Prankster during an explosion in the LexCorp Tower that Lex Luthor used to frame Superman, who was losing control of his powers due to Brainiac's Exobytes.

summary: Training Day is a story blog released on February 2025 on the game's website.

sections.title: Overview
items: Training Day is a story blog released on February 2025 on the game's website.
It serves as an epilogue to Day of Reckoning.

sections.title: Summary
items: The Atom and Green Lantern John Stewart are with Blue Lantern Esperanza and her twin sister Luzia of the Indigo Tribe at Esperanza's back yard for training (in microscopic sizes, for safety). Luzia demonstrates aptitude with her ring, and copying the abilities of other rings. Their session is interrupted when John is called away to Mogo's space sector due to a "Crisis situation", and Esperanza asks for permission to come along, as there is something important for her on Mogo. Luzia and the Atom watch them leave Earth.

sections.title: Trivia
items: This story blog features an art of John Stewart from the variant cover of Justice League Vol 4 #6 (2018) by Jim Lee, and an art of The Atom from the cover for the Legends of Tomorrow: The Atom 2018 collection, which is a remake of the cover for The Atom Special #1 (1993) by Steve Dillon.
The Atom mentions he once shrank Superboy, Supergirl, and Steel to save Superman. That happened during the crossover Superman: Critical Condition (2000).
The Atom mentions that he and John Stewart have both been Indigo Lanterns before, which occurred in the comics in the events Blackest Night (2009-2010) and Brightest Day (2010-2011).
Luzia and Esperanza are referred to as twins, but it was not specified if they were identical or sororal twins.
After the events of Hope Burns Bright, it is safe to say that the "something important" to Esperanza was SPOILER her daughter, Hope Cavalera.

title: Two-Face's Coin
summary: Two-Face's Coin is a rare, double-headed silver American dollar used by Two-Face to decide significant decisions on whether he should be virtuous and merciful or criminal and relentless.

sections.title: Overview
items: Two-Face's Coin is a rare, double-headed silver American dollar used by Two-Face to decide significant decisions on whether he should be virtuous and merciful or criminal and relentless.

sections.title: History
items: The two-headed coin was originally one of many which belonged to Harvey’s father, Christopher Dent; an alcoholic who would use the coin to psychologically and physically abuse Harvey; subjecting his son to a cruel game of "flipping the coin" on whether or not Harvey would be beaten. However, as Christopher always chose "heads" and Harvey, not knowing the the coin was double-sided, always chose "tails", Harvey always lost and got savagely beaten.

As a sign of love years later, Christopher, now a derelict drunk living in a run-down apartment with no memory of the “game” or his abuse, gave Harvey the coin as a gift; revealing to Harvey the game's injustice. Keeping the coin, Harvey quickly developed a habit of flipping the coin idly, especially when he became agitated.

During the trial of crime boss Maroni, the acid that the mobster threw at Dent also hit the coin in his pocket; scarring the exposed side. Dent used the coin's newly-given duality as the tie-breaker between his warring desires between light and dark. Following an initial rampage through Gotham, dealing justice as dictated by the coin, Dent finally confronted his father, he played the “game” with the new coin, however, as "Good Heads" came up, Two-Face let the old man live.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Two-Face's coin first appeared in Detective Comics #66 (August, 1942)

While Two-Face has possessed, and lost, a number of these coins over his criminal career, his psychosis makes him mark his coins in exactly the same way as the original coin; resulting in the coins being as identifiable to him as his fingerprints.

At one point, Two-Face was so dependent on the coin for any of his criminal acts that he could be easily defeated by taking the coin away from him or preventing him from seeing the result of the flip. Following psychological therapy, Dent has since lessened his dependency on the coin flip to whether a situation should be implemented, rather than each individual act.
Dent's coin is genuinely silver, as evidenced by one occasion when Two-Face used the coin to kill a werewolf.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The Batman is infamous for possessing a vast armada of vehicles custom built to tackle various terrains for various purposes.

Hal Jordan has a rebuilt Manhunter transport ship he found in a junkyard on Oa. He had Green Lantern Stel rebuild and reprogram it to serve as an emergency transport at the "Green House"; an emergency regroup point on an ice planet in Sector 2000. Dubbing it the "Interceptor", the ship possesses an autonomous A.I. named AYA, the ability to track Power Rings, and emergency escape pods should the need arise to abandon ship.
Nightwing and Arsenal's Outsiders team utilized a specialized battle cruiser, called a Pequod, as the team's primary mode of transportation between and during missions.

items: Villainy United is a boss team in the Arkham Asylum (Alert) instance. Players are tasked by Batman (heroes) and Joker (villains) to re-incarcerate them.

sections.title: Fight Mechanics
items: Scarecrow and Ivy will attack the player party at the same time.
Scarecrow uses One-Handed attacks and summons Rifle wielding Hallucinations of himself.
Ivy uses mostly Hand Blast attacks and summons Death Blossoms to attack the player party.

Throughout the fight Ivy will "teleport" herself around the stage via a plant that will pop up from the ground and swallow her, the plant will then disappear back into the ground and reappear behind the player to deposit Ivy who will renew her attack.
After Scarecrow and Ivy are defeated, Mister Freeze will attack the player party.

Freeze mostly uses Rifle attacks and periodically unleashes a devastating AOE attack (accompanied by a warning message), jumping to the center of the room and dealing high damage to anyone in line of sight - the entire group must hide behind one of the two pillars. After this, he will start dropping icicles in a random pattern.
